questions.why: A determiner in front of the noun forces c'est. Without the article the noun is bare, and then it is il est médecin.

questions.q: ___ difficile de parler français. (commenting in general)
questions.why: For the it of an unspecified situation, French uses c'est with a masculine singular adjective. Elle est difficile would describe one specific person or thing.
Savoir takes a clause or a question word; connaître takes a noun and is never followed by a clause. Je connais Paris, but je sais où il habite.
A familiar thing, so connaître. Note the pair from Part II: j'ai su means I found out, j'ai connu means I met.
Counted with a number, use the short form: ans. Described as a whole span, use the long one: année. Same logic for jour / journée and soir / soirée.
The whole span, experienced, so the long form. Je pars dans trois jours, counted, takes the short one.

choices: J'apporte mon frère à la fête.
J'amène mon frère à la fête.
J'emporte mon frère à la fête.
J'emmène le gâteau à la fête.
questions.why: Two axes: amener / emmener for people, apporter / emporter for things; a- forms bring towards, em- forms take away.

questions.q: ___ ton parapluie. (take it away with you)
questions.why: A thing, taken away, so emporter. Apporte would mean bring it here.

questions.q: How do you say « I miss you » ?
questions.why: Manquer reverses the roles: literally, you are lacking to me. Je te manque means the opposite, that you miss me.
Plaire works like manquer: the thing liked is the subject. Tu lui plais means he or she likes you.

choices: Je visite ma tante. / Je rends visite à Paris.
Je rends visite à ma tante. / Je visite Paris.
Je visite à ma tante. / Je rends visite Paris.
Je visite ma tante. / Je visite Paris.
questions.why: Visiter is for places; a person gets rendre visite à. Saying je visite ma tante sounds like an inspection.
Jouer de for an instrument, jouer à for a game: je joue du piano, je joue au tennis.

questions.q: « Actuellement, il est en France. » What does actuellement mean?
questions.why: Actuellement means currently; actually is en fait. Its neighbour éventuellement means possibly, not eventually, which is finalement.
Three words, and the subject is the person being missed. Reason it as you are missed by me.

questions.q: Why should you never say « Je suis excité » or « Je suis plein » ? Give the correct alternatives.
a: Je suis excité means sexually aroused, not excited: say j'ai hâte or je suis impatient. Je suis plein means drunk (or pregnant, of an animal), not full after a meal: say j'ai bien mangé or je n'ai plus faim.
questions.why: These are the two false friends in the chapter that cost you more than accuracy. Both come from translating the English adjective directly.
